findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Upon arrival paper towels were not available at the designated handwashing sink. PIC stated they used the handwashing sink but then used napkins located in a different part of the kitchen to dry their hands. This meant the handwashing sink was shut off without a barrier prior to drying hands. Also, a person on-site helping in the kitchen was observed not using proper technique and also shut off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. Ensure all staff are using proper technique during handwashing. Educational handout on proper handwashing technique was provided.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

Thorough cleaning and sanitizing of dish machine is needed prior to use.
2) Grimy buildup and dust accumulation were observed along the upper edge of the ice scoop holder. Sides and bottom inside the ice scoop holder were also soiled with mold and rust colored debris/accumulation. Ice scoop holder and scoops were cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
3) Mildew and juice splash were observed on inner surfaces of the juice machine and on surfaces around dispensing heads. Surfaces were wiped down with bleach solution after breakfast service.  
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 Chemical jug of sanitizer connected to dish machine was empty. Another open jug was light in color and appeared to be diluted. Fresh jug of sanitizer was connected to the dish machine. Chlorine final rinse concentration was observed at 0ppm after the line was primed to allow for proper dispensing of chemical. Several cycles were ran with the same result. The dish machine is not functioning properly and needs to be serviced. Machine was taken out of service, and maintenance noted they would shut off the breaker until repairs were completed. Three part sink was setup and used for ware washing, and bleach solution at 100-200pppm was used for sanitization. Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration at 50-200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration.

Clean in the aforementioned areas and throughout the kitchen daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Walls were observed peeling and with disrepair in the dish area around the dish machine, under the sprayer sink, along the top of the base coving, and around/under the 3 part sink. Provide repairs to the walls in the dish area.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) working during the inspection. Ensure a CFPM is working during all hours of food preparation and food service. Additionally, when workers get the CFPM license, make sure a certificate is available.  

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There were no paper towels located at the hand sink in the kitchen during the inspection. Ensure paper towels are stocked and available at all times to ensure employees can properly dry their hands. Paper towels were stocked during the inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine was not working properly. The chlorine sanitizer concentration was 0ppm. Ensure the dish machine is serviced so the sanitizer concentration is maintained at the proper concentration. Dishes must be sanitized in the 3 part sink until the dish machine is serviced. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
There was no sanitizer bucket being used during the inspection. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is made and used during all hours of food preparation and service. Also, make sure wiping cloths are held in sanitizer between use. The kitchen worker stated he will use sanitizer buckets from now on. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There were multiple holes on the wall near the 3 part sink. Ensure these holes are sealed so the wall is smooth and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The wall behind the dish machine was soiled with mold. Ensure the walls are cleaned as frequently as necessary so they are maintained clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mops were stored sitting in the mop sink and mop bucket. This is not proper storage. Mops must be stored in a position that allows them to air dry without contaminating equipment. Also, wastewater in the mop bucket had not been discarded since the last use. Ensure wastewater in the mop bucket is discarded after use. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: The manager’s CFM certificate was not available during the inspection. Ensure a certificate is provided to the inspector during the inspection. 
(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: Observed the spatula being used to be old with cracks and gouges in it, which makes it not easily cleaned. The spatula was discarded during the inspection. Ensure all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. 
Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion.
